doc.title: Marian McPartland interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, April 26, 1997

title: Finding guests: Frank Kimbrough, Tony Monte, Stevie Wonder
summary: Choosing future guests, including those she has not yet reached.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: So now that you’ve done so many fine musicians, is it more of a challenge to find people to do these days, or is there constantly a new selection to choose from?

Well both. I just thought of the guy’s name, I should give him a name, the guy that plays in Maria Schneider’s band, Frank Kimbrough, and he’s somebody you’re definitely going to hear about. But in answer to your question, well it’s both. There still are a lot of people out there that I probably should have asked but for whatever reason, there’s just too many of them, like I just got around to calling up somebody named Tony Monte do you know him?

Monte. M-O-N-T-E. He’s been around the New York scene for years, a really good player. And just somehow I never got to it. And then of course there’s people I would like to have and probably never can like Stevie Wonder. I mean to get through to him I’d probably have to get in a plane and fly over his house and drop a note or something.
That would get his attention I think.
Well maybe. I’d better do something, because he’s a person that would be a really good show and I know all his tunes, or enough of them.
